A build-along course

Building Halfpast

A booking platform that tells the truth: which times are free, in whose time zone, and what happens when two people tap the same eleven o'clock at the same moment. Built from an empty folder to a tested, deployable app.

35 chapters SvelteKit 3 RCSvelte 5 asyncNode 24 LTSDrizzle + libSQL
Start chapter 01 →

Everything we'll cover

  1. 01 What we are building A booking platform, and an honest look at the two things that make one hard.
  2. 02 How the pieces fit A map of the app before we write any of it.
  3. 03 Node, pnpm and the floor Getting the right runtime, and making the project refuse the wrong one.
  4. 04 Scaffolding the project One command, and a tour of what it produced.
  5. 05 Three kinds of time Instants, calendar dates and wall-clock readings are three different things. Mixing them up is the source of nearly every scheduling bug.
  6. 06 A date library that knows about places Installing @internationalized/date, and the four types that map onto the three kinds of time.
  7. 07 The five-minute grid Turning "do these two appointments overlap?" — a question with a dozen edge cases — into "is this cell taken?", which has none.
  8. 08 The availability engine Recurring rules plus a full diary plus the shape of a service, in — every bookable start time, out. No database, no clock.
  9. 09 Testing time with Vitest Setting up Vitest properly, then writing the tests that would otherwise take six months to run.
  10. 10 A database in a file SQLite through libSQL and Drizzle, and the two pragmas that decide whether it can serve a website at all.
  11. 11 The schema Nine tables, two storage conventions, and the snapshots that keep last year’s receipts honest.
  12. 12 The line that stops double-booking The whole concurrency problem, solved by a primary key. This is the most important chapter in the course.
  13. 13 Migrations and seed data Turning the schema into actual tables, and building a demo studio you can throw away and rebuild in a second.
  14. 14 One writer at a time The SQLITE_BUSY error, why the obvious fix deadlocks in Node, and a nine-line queue that does not.
  15. 15 Configuration without magic SvelteKit 3 deleted `svelte.config.js` and the `$env` modules. What replaced them is better, and stricter.
  16. 16 Who are you Better Auth for staff, a bearer token in an email for customers, and why those are different problems.
  17. 17 Guards that throw Authorisation in one file, with a deliberate choice of status code for each kind of refusal.
  18. 18 Taking a booking The one function that writes an appointment, and the four things it does in order.
  19. 19 Telling everyone something changed A tiny publish/subscribe module built on async generators — the engine behind the live diary.
  20. 20 Functions that cross the network `query` and `command`: server code you import into a component and call like any other function.
  21. 21 Forms that work without JavaScript `form()`, `fields.<name>.as()`, and the rule that catches everybody once.
  22. 22 Live queries `query.live` takes an async generator. Three lines of shape, and the receptionist’s screen updates itself.
  23. 23 Async Svelte, and its sharp edges `await` inside `$derived`, boundaries with pending and failed snippets, and two traps that cost this project an afternoon each.
  24. 24 A design system in plain CSS Tokens in oklch, a fluid type scale that respects zoom, and dark mode as an exercise in flipping numbers.
  25. 25 The booking page Service, person, day, time, details — in one page that survives a refresh and works without JavaScript.
  26. 26 The slot grid The one component customers actually touch. Radio buttons in disguise, sized for thumbs.
  27. 27 The customer’s own page One link, no account, and a cancel button that respects the studio’s notice period.
  28. 28 The live diary The screen a receptionist stares at all day. Today by default, updating itself, readable across a room.
  29. 29 The owner’s screens Services, hours, team and settings — four small forms with one thing each to teach.
  30. 30 Motion with a job GSAP loaded on demand, gated on reduced motion, and used only where movement carries information.
  31. 31 Mobile first, for real Breakpoints that come from the content, tap targets that fit a thumb, and the viewport units that actually work.
  32. 32 Unit tests that earn their keep What to test, what not to, and the concurrency test that is the most valuable one in the project.
  33. 33 End-to-end tests Playwright against a real build, with fixtures that make every test independent — and selectors that break for the right reasons.
  34. 34 A security pass Walking the app the way somebody hostile would, with a checklist rather than a vibe.
  35. 35 Shipping it The build, the environment, the one adapter setting that ruins your day, and what to check afterwards.

Every chapter shows the real code from the finished project in halfpast-app. Type it out rather than pasting where you can — the errors you make and fix are the part that sticks.
